title: Supreme Court Dismisses 'Cheap Publicity' Plea Seeking Criminal Probe Against Justice Varma
excerpt: The bench rejected the petition calling for an FIR and SIT investigation into the unaccounted cash controversy involving Delhi High Court's former judge Yashwant Varma.
body:
• Supreme Court dismissed a petition seeking a criminal probe into Justice Yashwant Varma's unaccounted cash controversy, calling it a bid for "cheap publicity."
  • The bench refused to order an FIR or SIT investigation, saying existing mechanisms were adequate to handle the matter.
  • Justice Varma had faced scrutiny after large amounts of unaccounted cash were allegedly found during a fire incident at his residence.
  • The court's ruling effectively closes one avenue of legal challenge, though the expert panel review continues.

The Supreme Court of India on Thursday dismissed a public interest petition seeking a criminal investigation into the unaccounted cash controversy involving Justice Yashwant Varma, a former judge of the Delhi High Court, terming the plea an exercise in "cheap publicity."

Court Rejects Calls for FIR and SIT Probe

A bench of the Supreme Court refused to entertain the petition that had demanded the registration of a First Information Report and the constitution of a Special Investigation Team to probe the matter. The petitioner had argued that the discovery of large amounts of unaccounted cash at Justice Varma's residence warranted a full criminal investigation beyond the internal judicial mechanisms already in place.

The court, however, was unsparing in its assessment of the petition's motivations. The bench observed that the plea appeared designed to generate publicity rather than advance any legitimate legal grievance, and noted that existing institutional frameworks were equipped to address the allegations.

"This petition is nothing but an attempt at cheap publicity."

— Supreme Court bench, dismissing the plea

The Unaccounted Cash Controversy

The controversy surrounding Justice Varma dates back to an incident at his official residence, where a fire led to the discovery of what was described as a substantial amount of unaccounted cash. The incident triggered calls for an investigation from multiple quarters, including lawyers' bodies and opposition politicians who questioned how a sitting High Court judge could possess such funds.

Following the discovery, the Supreme Court had referred the matter to an expert committee for review. The committee's proceedings have remained largely confidential, in keeping with established practice for judicial conduct inquiries. Questions have been raised in Parliament about whether the expert panel's report will be tabled during the current session.

Judicial Accountability Under Scrutiny

The dismissal of the petition does not end all proceedings related to Justice Varma. The expert panel constituted by the Supreme Court continues its work, and its findings could still have significant consequences. However, the court's refusal to allow a parallel criminal track signals its preference for handling judicial misconduct allegations through established internal mechanisms rather than the criminal justice system.

Legal experts have noted that the Supreme Court has historically been cautious about subjecting sitting or former judges to criminal investigations, preferring to use the in-house procedure established under its own guidelines. Critics argue this approach lacks transparency, while defenders say it protects judicial independence from politically motivated complaints.

The case has drawn attention across India and among the Indian diaspora, where concerns about judicial integrity and institutional accountability remain a recurring theme in discussions about governance and the rule of law.

The Supreme Court's order is final and cannot be appealed, effectively closing the criminal probe demand. All eyes now turn to the expert panel's findings and whether they will be made public.
